subject.title: [Feature]: bearer token authentication for proxy servers

question: Which native mobile reverse-proxy transport-auth contract should OpenClaw support before implementation: static bearer/Basic/header fields only, OIDC browser handoff too, or no native proxy credentials for now?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the durable boundary controls pre-Gateway credentials, mobile storage, setup-code metadata, and OIDC redirect handling, so automation should not choose it alone.

options.title: Approve staged static proxy auth
options.body: Define bearer, Basic, and fixed-header fields first with strict credential lifecycle, TLS, redaction, setup-code, Android, and iOS requirements, leaving OIDC for a later design.

options.title: Design the full proxy-auth suite
options.body: Cover static headers, cookies, and OIDC together before implementation, accepting a broader design and validation cycle.

options.title: Decline native proxy credentials
options.body: Document authenticated reverse proxies as unsupported for native mobile clients and recommend VPN, tunnel, WebChat, or proxy configuration alternatives.

recommendation.title: Approve staged static proxy auth
recommendation.body: Define bearer, Basic, and fixed-header fields first with strict credential lifecycle, TLS, redaction, setup-code, Android, and iOS requirements, leaving OIDC for a later design.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current setup-code and Gateway auth contract history, and this decision is primarily about the security boundary before platform implementation.
